Hi, I'm Edward King

Software Engineer & Educator, M.Ed.

I bring a balance of creativity, technical skill, organization, and clear, effective communication to every project I take on — whether that's shipping code or running a classroom.

Contact: ed.king4967@gmail.com

About Me

Hi there! I'm a teacher and software engineer with 12 years of combined experience, and I've never quite been able to choose just one craft — so I didn't.

Building things

I spent five years as an engineer working mostly in C++, JavaScript, Python, and Flask — time split between a NetApp internship and later a full-time firmware role, CU Space Grant (where I helped build the power system for the DANDE research satellite), a water-infrastructure project with NapoNet, and In‑Situ. On the side, I built a 3D game demo, Monk vs Ninjas, just to see if I could.

Teaching

I taught for five years across engineering, math, ESL, English, creative writing, film, and computer science — after two years of substitute teaching to make sure it was really what I wanted. It was: I went on to earn a master's degree in Education and student taught in a wonderfully diverse high school. These days I teach AP Computer Science and Engineering full time.

Writing & performing

I created and led A Thousand and One Stories, a literary journal I built from scratch — designing the site, writing plugins in HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, managing submissions, editing, hiring a small team of editors, and forming an LLC to handle payments. We published over 100 stories from authors around the world. Writing runs through the rest of my life too: I hold an English bachelor's degree alongside my engineering one, completed an honors thesis in Creative Writing, had nine stories published and four plays performed, and played music in three rock bands and a high school jazz band — occasionally taking original songs to open mic nights.

Travel, language & adventure

I taught ESL in Suzhou, China for a year and in Madrid, Spain for a semester, and worked as a Spanish–English translator on a trip to Napo, Peru, assessing whether an existing telecom network could be repurposed for education. I studied Chinese for two semesters, including one at Xi'an Jiaotong University, and I now speak both Spanish and Chinese. When I'm not working, I'm usually looking for the next climb or cliff walk — so far that's included Long's Peak and the famously vertigo-inducing plank walk of Hua Shan.
